purpose: Step B prerequisite: candidate CLT inject/suppress features for the means-ends action tokens, from a full vocab scan of the 2.5M Gemma CLT. Determines whether the locked on_off cell can be steered.

scan.metric: decoder -> embedding cosine; Gemma ties embeddings, so this is the feature's logit-write direction toward the token

caveat: Candidates only. Final steering efficacy is validated by the Step B suppress-plus-inject sweep (as in COLM); cosine is a necessary, not sufficient, indicator. COLM's working 2.5M inject features were ~0.4-0.6.

closed.verdict: UNUSABLE - no clean feature (polysemantic open/close-ness; #1 token is 'opened')

step_b_decision.rationale: Only family with clean, single-sense features on BOTH sides (on 0.51, off 0.36), enabling bidirectional suppress-plus-inject. 'open' is the single cleanest action feature (0.54) but 'closed' has no usable feature (0.15), so open_closed cannot do a clean bidirectional intervention. up/down are usable but weak (0.26-0.31) - a secondary fallback.
step_b_decision.note: The off feature is weaker than on, so the redirect may need asymmetric/higher strength on the off side; the Step B sweep will quantify. Both features sit at L24-25 (late), consistent with the COLM Gemma redirect features.
